key_events.summary: The interim US-Iran ceasefire collapsed after Iranian attacks on Gulf shipping; Trump declared the truce 'over' and US forces resumed strikes on Iran, reigniting the war (which the US and Israel launched on Feb. 28) and pushing oil prices up.
May CPI showed annual inflation jumping to 4.2% (from 3.8%), a three-year high driven by war-related energy costs; Trump drew criticism for saying he 'loves' the inflation numbers.

Trump and Iranian President Pezeshkian signed a memorandum of understanding meant to end the Iran war (signed by Trump at Versailles after the G7), trading sanctions relief for uranium dilution and a 60-day window for a final deal.

Trump said US strikes on Iran would not resume before the Nov. 3 midterms, while directing the Pentagon to prepare options for renewed combat, including a short, intense multi-day strike campaign (per NYT reporting).

At the GOP's midterm convention in Dallas, Trump promised a $5,000 'Trump Dividend' to every US adult if Republicans keep both chambers; the plan would cost over $1 trillion and need congressional approval, and its legality was questioned.
The Federal Reserve raised its policy rate by a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00%, citing elevated inflation, making borrowing costlier heading into the election.

The Supreme Court, for the third time, refused to let Missouri use its new GOP-drawn map in 2026, leaving the 2022 map in place for November despite the new lines having been used in the August primaries; voters will decide the new map's fate by referendum.
The Supreme Court (6-3) let Alabama use a Republican-drawn congressional map that eliminates one of its two majority-Black districts, likely costing Democrats a seat.
Florida's Supreme Court declined to block the new DeSantis-drawn congressional map, so a plan making 24 of 28 seats GOP-leaning (up to four Republican pickups) will be used in 2026.
Maine Democratic Senate nominee Graham Platner quit the race against Sen. Susan Collins after a sexual assault allegation, forcing Democrats to pick a replacement in a must-win Senate state.
Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC) died suddenly at 71; Gov. McMaster appointed his sister Darline Graham, who was sworn in July 14, and a special GOP primary was scheduled to pick a new nominee.

The administration imposed new 10%-12.5% tariffs on goods from 60 trading partners (covering nearly all US imports), citing forced-labor enforcement after the Supreme Court had struck down many emergency-power tariffs earlier in the year.
Trump signed a stopgap spending bill (House vote 370-48 on Sept. 1) funding the government through Dec. 11, averting an Oct. 1 shutdown before the midterms.
key_events.date_note: Ballotpedia News says signed Sept. 3; Wikipedia (citing Reuters, which blocked access) says Sept. 2.

key_events.summary: The Supreme Court refused the administration's request to enforce new Postal Service restrictions on mail ballots, likely ending efforts to curtail mail voting for the midterms.
The Supreme Court struck down Trump's executive order limiting birthright citizenship, a major legal defeat for his agenda.
In a GOP-backed case (NRSC v. FEC), the Supreme Court erased federal limits on party spending coordinated with candidates, reshaping campaign finance for the midterms.
After trade talks collapsed, the US imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion of Canadian goods and Canada vowed dollar-for-dollar retaliation.
Trump signed a party-line (214-212 House vote) ~$70 billion ICE and Border Patrol funding law, ending a nearly six-month fight over DHS funding that had produced a record-long DHS shutdown.

At a Nebraska rally, Trump said Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego while calling high war-driven gas prices a small price to pay, drawing sharp criticism, especially from California Democrats; the White House said he meant the war prevents such threats.
Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 storm, leaving hundreds of thousands without power in the Florida Panhandle and Alabama less than four weeks before the election.
US national debt passed $40 trillion, while long-term Treasury yields rose to their highest in nearly 20 years.

key_events_note: Events list built from Wikipedia '2026 in the United States' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_in_the_United_States, last edited 2026-10-11) plus the linked news articles opened individually. importance_rank is a subjective analyst ranking; take ranks 1-12 for a ~12-item list. Background (before window): US-Israel war on Iran began 2026-02-28; two 2026 shutdowns (Jan 31-Feb 3 partial; DHS-only Feb 14-Apr 30, longest ever).

redistricting_net_effect.summary: Maps actually in effect for Nov 2026 imply a nominal net shift of about R+9 seats (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia); Cook Political Report's likeliest realized effect is about R+4. Missouri (R+1) and Virginia (D+4) changes are NOT in effect for 2026.

notes: WebSearch quota was exhausted partway through (per coordinating agent); later items were found via links inside opened pages (mainly Wikipedia reference lists) rather than new searches.

Blocked/unavailable: reuters.com (HTTP 401), fox59.com (403), centerforpolitics.org Sabato's Crystal Ball (403), bls.gov pages via curl (403). BLS numbers were read with WebFetch (twice) and cross-checked against the official BLS public API (api.bls.gov). No paywalls/bot-blocks were circumvented.
Cook Political Report tracker body is subscriber-only; only the free summary was used (R net about 4).

House: Kevin Kiley is officially an Independent who caucuses with Republicans, so the GOP-aligned bloc is 219 vs 214 Democrats. Some sources (Wikipedia summary tables) count him as R; Ballotpedia's '218-212 with four vacancies' is outdated.
Louisiana US House: primaries on Nov 3 and general election on Dec 12, 2026, so LA House results will not be final on Election Night.

Missouri: the 2025 map was used in the Aug 4 primaries but the 2022 map governs the November general election (SCOTUS 2026-09-25), so nominees may run in districts that differ from where they were nominated.
Stopgap funding signing date: Ballotpedia News says Sept 3, 2026; Wikipedia (citing Reuters) says Sept 2. Recorded as Sept 3.

Inflation path: CPI y/y peaked at 4.2% in May 2026 (BBC on June 10 release) and was 3.4% in August 2026 (BLS). September CPI is due 2026-10-14 and Q3 GDP advance estimate 2026-10-29 (before Election Day); the October jobs report is due 2026-11-06 (after).
UMich sentiment (46.3 prelim Oct) is near historic lows; the page links the inflation-expectations jump to the Iran conflict that began in February.
Trump approval ratings were not collected in this pass.

Tariff legal history: NBC (2026-06-30) refers to a February 2026 Supreme Court ruling invalidating the sweeping tariffs, while an AP article (2026-09-10) says 'last year'. Unresolved; not used as a data point.
Event summaries are paraphrased; importance_rank is a judgment call.
